title: PID-Controlled Elevator
summary: A model elevator that moves between floors under closed-loop PID control, with homing, a request queue and end stops.
problem: Move an elevator cab to requested floors accurately and smoothly, and serve several requests in the order they arrive.
approach: An ultrasonic sensor measures cab height, limit switches set the floor positions, and LabVIEW running on National Instruments DAQ hardware closes a PID loop on a geared motor through a PWM servo amplifier. Floor requests go into a first-in, first-out queue. We started from the equations of motion, 3D-printed the mounts and cab parts, and tested in stages: sensors alone, manual control, a PD controller on a setpoint, auto homing, then full floor sequences, with end stops added as a safeguard.
result: The elevator positioned reliably under closed-loop control and ran homing, queued floor sequences and end-stop tests (see the videos). The main limit was the DAQ hardware’s analog, digital and counter channels. Next steps: more precise position sensing, less vibration, more floors and smarter scheduling.
